summary: Permanently retire an agent identity and refuse fresh sends at the serialized writer fence.

replay.detail: No upgrade-wide replay is required. Terminal retirement projects immediately; replay and reopen preserve precedence over later declarations. Replicated sends remain accepted history.

schema.detail: Register durable agent.retired with optional reserved successor/transfer fields; registry digest changes. Startup installs partial retained-lifecycle and per-subject lifecycle-operation indexes and keyed desired-selection triggers; no numeric core storage-version bump.

rules.detail: Retention rules digest changes to retain agent.retired durably. Retirement permanently prevents revival; exact accepted send retries precede admission and fresh sends refuse once local graph knows retirement.

compatibility.detail: Add client-v0 agent.retire, retired agent state, recipient-retired/lifecycle-unavailable/retirement-upgrade-required errors with applied none. Old registries retain unknown kinds/fields retryably but cannot enforce retirement. Old client error decoders preserve generic messages. See docs/st3/agent-retirement.md.

manual.detail: Upgrade every configured/active member together before terminal retirement. Creation is disabled until all peers have advertised the matching registry digest. Prevent member downgrade afterward and upgrade new members before admission; use agent.retire at the declaring host with explicit actor, reason and idempotency key.

recovery.detail: Roll forward after retirement; do not downgrade members that must enforce the new claim. Identity retirement is permanent. Durable terminal records and preaccepted messages survive replay and import; custody transfer remains deferred.

downtime.detail: Normal coordinated daemon restart; restart duration and deployed fleet performance have not been measured.
